quarterly_data.signal: Bloom released a special report, 'The New Rules of AI Power', arguing that its solid oxide fuel cells generate continuous 800V DC power natively, removing AC-to-DC conversion stages and reducing dependence on transformers and switchgear. The company's own economic analysis (its 800V DC Total Cost of Ownership model for a 1 GW compute data center using next-generation AI rack assumptions; 'Actual project economics will vary') claims a reduction of non-compute CAPEX by $3.6 billion, or 27%, and of five-year total cost of ownership by $5.5 billion, or 9%, versus competing traditional AC solutions. CMO Natalie Sunderland: 'We're seeing the shift to 800V DC happen faster than many expected'; Bloom's 2026 Mid-Year Data Center Power Report found data center leaders expect DC-based architectures to account for 58% of new deployments by 2030. CEO KR Sridhar called Bloom 'the industry leader in ushering in this new era' (company claim).
